questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To flog a dead horse'

options.text: Beat an animal to carry goods
Waste time on lost cause
Complain loudly and cry
Work hard and win a prize

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Waste time on lost cause.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To flog a dead horse"** means to waste time and effort on something that has no chance of succeeding or is already a lost cause. (खोए हुए कारण पर समय बर्बाद करना)

 
 
• **Example: **Trying to convince him to change his mind is like flogging a dead horse; he’s already made his decision.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom suggests putting effort into something that has no hope of yielding results.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

questions.question:
Change the following from active to passive:

She was driving the car when the accident occurred.

options.text: The car is being driven by her when the accident occurred.
The car had been driven by her when the accident occurred.
The car was being driven by her when the accident occurred.
She had driven the car when the accident occurred.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 

• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence. 

• In the active voice, the sentence is: "She was driving the car when the accident occurred." 

• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the car" at the beginning. 

• Change the active verb form "was driving" to "was being driven" (past continuous passive). 

• Retain the time phrase "when the accident occurred" as it is essential to the sentence meaning. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**. 
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The car was being driven by her when the accident occurred."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
 

• **Option 1: **"The car is being driven by her when the accident occurred." – Incorrect tense (present continuous passive). 

• **Option 2: **"The car had been driven by her when the accident occurred." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive). 

• **Option 4: **"She had driven the car when the accident occurred." – Incorrect voice (active voice).

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

He said, "I am reading a book now."

options.text: He said that he is reading a book then.
He said that he was reading a book now.
He said that he was reading a book then.
He said that he had read a book then.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He said that he was reading a book then.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• Direct speech pronoun "I" is changed to "he" in indirect speech to match the subject of the reporting clause.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change:**
 
 
• Present continuous tense "am reading" is changed to past continuous tense "was reading" in indirect speech to indicate a past event.
 
 
 
• **Time Reference:**
 
 
• The word "now" in direct speech is changed to "then" in indirect speech to reflect the appropriate time reference.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Indirect speech does not use quotation marks and modifies the sentence structure accordingly.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *He said that he was reading a book then.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "He said that he is reading a book then."
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "is reading" should change to "was reading" in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "He said that he was reading a book now."
 
 
• Incorrect time reference: "now" should change to "then" in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He said that he had read a book then."
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "had read" implies a past perfect action, which does not match the original meaning of the sentence.
 
 
</ul

The officer ordered the soldiers to march forward.

options.text: The officer said to the soldiers, "March forward."
The officer asked the soldiers, "You must march now."
The officer asked, "Would you march forward?"
The officer order, "Marching forward now!"

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The officer ordered the soldiers to march forward.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"ordered the soldiers to march" becomes "said to the soldiers, 'March forward.'"**
 
 
• The reporting verb "ordered" is converted to "said to" with the imperative statement "March forward."
 
• The imperative statement in indirect speech is directly quoted in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "March" and ends with a period "."
 
• Reporting clause precedes the quoted speech, separated by a comma.
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The officer said to the soldiers, 'March forward.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This changes the tone of the sentence from a command to a suggestion or a request, which is not accurate.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "The officer asked, 'Would you march forward?'"
 
 
• This changes the command to a question, altering the meaning of the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "The officer order, 'Marching forward now!'"
 
 
• Contains grammatical errors: "order" should be "ordered," and the structure is not suitable for direct speech.

questions.question:
Arrange the parts to form a correct sentence:

(1) He sowed the seeds

(2) The sprouts began to appear

(3) The farmer ploughed the field

(4) He watered the seeds sown in the field
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (1)** i.e. **3 → 1 → 4 → 2**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sequence logically begins with **part (3)**: "The farmer ploughed the field," which is the necessary preparation step.
 
• Next comes **part (1)**: "He sowed the seeds," which follows ploughing and places the seeds in the prepared soil.
 
• Then **part (4)**: "He watered the seeds sown in the field," which supports germination after sowing.
 
• Finally **part (2)**: "The sprouts began to appear," which is the natural result after sowing and watering.

Therefore, the correct answer is **3 → 1 → 4 → 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (1 → 3 → 4 → 2):** Starts with sowing before ploughing, which is illogical because the field must be prepared first.

questions.question:
Arrange the parts to form a correct sentence:

(1) They revised thoroughly.

(2) The test was challenging.

(3) Their preparation paid off.

(4) Most of them scored well.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (1)** i.e. **1 → 2 → 3 → 4**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Start with **part (1)**: "They revised thoroughly." — this establishes the students' action before the test.
 
• Follow with **part (2)**: "The test was challenging." — introduces the difficulty they faced.
 
• Then **part (3)**: "Their preparation paid off." — shows the result of their revision despite the challenge.
 
• End with **part (4)**: "Most of them scored well." — the final outcome of preparation and effort.

Therefore, the correct answer is **1 → 2 → 3 → 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (2 → 1 → 3 → 4):** Begins with the test being challenging before mentioning revision, which disrupts the cause-effect flow.
 
• **Option 3 (1 → 2 → 4 → 3):** Places the outcome "Most of them scored well" before stating that "Their preparation paid off," which reverses the logical explanation.
 
• **Option 4 (1 → 3 → 2 → 4):** Claims preparation paid off before mentioning the test's difficulty, weakening the contrast that makes the result meaningful.

questions.question: Select the correct Synonym of 'IMPECUNIOUS'.

options.text: Wealthy
Generous
Poor
Frugal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **Poor**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Impecunious"** means having little or no money; being poor or penniless. (निर्धन)

 
 
• **Example:** The impecunious student struggled to pay his tuition fees.
 
 
 
• **"Poor"** refers to having little or no wealth or material possessions. It conveys the same meaning as "impecunious." (गरीब)
 
 
• **Example:** Many charities work to provide assistance to poor families in need.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the synonym of **'impecunious'** is **'poor.'**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Wealthy** (धनी): Having a lot of money or valuable possessions.

 
 
• **Example:** The wealthy businessman donated a large sum of money to the orphanage.
 
 
 
• **Generous** (उदार): Willing to give or share more than is necessary or expected, especially in terms of money or kindness.
 
 
• **Example:** She is known for being generous with her time and resources.
 
 
 
• **Frugal** (मितव्ययी): Economical in use or spending; avoiding waste.
 
 
• **Example:** He lived a frugal life, saving most of his income for future needs.
